findings.problem: The group-law cancellation argument (idempotent implies identity), together with its corollaries `inv_one`, `nsmulPt_one` and `pushPt_one_of_hom`, is copied verbatim into at least three files. These are the `_of_charZero` sibling (lines 25–52) and `exists_fakeEllipticCurve_one_isPullback_and_act_eq_of_act_of_algHom_matrix_of_trace` (lines 415–442). `eq_one_of_mul_self` is also re-proved in a dozen or more other Sol files. This is real algebra: cancel `inv x` on the left of `x * x = x`. It is not routine unfolding. A fix to any one copy, or a change to the `RelativeGroupLaw` API, has to be made by hand in each of them.
findings.proposed_change: Move these four lemmas once into the module that defines `RelativeGroupLaw` (or its `Prod` file, which this file already imports), as `RelativeGroupLaw.eq_one_of_mul_self`, `RelativeGroupLaw.inv_one`, `RelativeGroupLaw.nsmulPt_one` and `RelativeGroupLaw.pushPt_one_of_hom`. Keep the statements and calc proof exactly as at lines 25–52. Delete the local copies and call the shared lemmas. In `main`, the uses become `L2.inv_one t` (currently `inv_one L2 t`), `L2.nsmulPt_one t 1` and `L2.pushPt_one_of_hom (act x) (hact x) (fun t P Q => hhom x t P Q) t`. The same replacements apply in the sibling files, since their hypotheses are identical (`{S} [CommRing S] {A} {f} (L : RelativeGroupLaw S f)`).
findings.benefit: There is one proof of the idempotent-is-identity argument instead of many near-identical ones. The Sol files shrink and their remaining content (the actual QM construction) is easier to see. Any later change to `RelativeGroupLaw` axioms needs only one edit.

findings.problem: The characterisation of points factoring through the unit section (`unitSection`, `unitSection_comp`, `factorsThrough_unitSection_iff`) and the fibre-dimension computation `topologicalKrullDim_fibre_eq` are copied verbatim into the sibling `_of_charZero` file (lines 54–87) and into the `exists_fakeEllipticCurve_one_isPullback...` file (lines 444–477). The `FactorsThrough` proof is a non-trivial argument that uses naturality of `one`, a `congrArg` on `≫ f`, and `Subtype.ext`. The fibre-dimension proof uses subsingleton Spec of a field, `Set.univ` and the homeomorphism invariance of Krull dimension. They are generic facts about a relative group law and about smooth schemes over a field. Nothing in them depends on the quaternionic setting.
findings.proposed_change: Put `RelativeGroupLaw.unitSection`, `unitSection_comp` and `factorsThrough_unitSection_iff` in the `RelativeGroupLaw` development, unchanged. Put `topologicalKrullDim_fibre_eq` next to the `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` topological-dimension lemmas that it imports (`..._le_topologicalKrullDim` and `..._topologicalKrullDim_le`). In `main`, replace `unitSection L2` and `(factorsThrough_unitSection_iff L2 t _).2 rfl` by the shared names. The `dim_fibre` field is then filled by `fun s => topologicalKrullDim_fibre_eq (prodStr f f) 2 (L2.unitSection) s`. Apply the same one-line renames in the two sibling files, whose variable context is identical.
findings.benefit: The unit-section and fibre-dimension machinery is stated and proved once. Each Sol file then only contains its own construction, and there is no risk that the copies drift apart. It also gives the `FactorsThrough` characterisation a discoverable, reusable home.
